searchDocs.title: Install by hand in Studio
searchDocs.content: Install by hand in Studio Download Init.rbxm from the latest release.In Studio, make a Folder named Packages in ReplicatedStorage. Drag Init.rbxm onto it (or right-click it › Insert from File).Make a Script named InitServer in ServerScriptService and paste in InitServer.Make a LocalScript named InitClient in StarterPlayer › StarterPlayerScripts and paste in InitClient.Make the folders the boot scripts name: in ReplicatedStorage Network, Services, Controllers, Binders (with Shared and Client inside); in ServerScriptService Services and Binders.Press Play and look for ✅ Initialized in the Output. The plugin's Setup button does all of this for you.

searchDocs.title: Adding your own folder​
searchDocs.content: Say you want ReplicatedStorage.Systems with modules named ...System:  Make the folder. Add an entry to InitServer and InitClient (or just one, if it's one-sided): { Folders = { ReplicatedStorage.Systems }, Predicate = Init.matchesName("System$") },

searchDocs.title: Attributes​
searchDocs.content: Set these on a ModuleScript in the Properties window:  Attribute	Type	EffectIgnore	boolean	true: Init skips it Priority	number	lower loads earlier inside its entry (default 0)

searchDocs.title: The old Entries modules​
searchDocs.content: The old Init kept entries in SharedEntries/ServerEntries/ClientEntries modules as named dictionaries with Order. That format still works: Init.start(require(path.to.ServerEntries)) sorts it by Order. See Migrating.

searchDocs.title: Add your first module​
searchDocs.content: Click the Services folder in ServerScriptService.Press Service in the plugin. A new module opens.Rename it in the Explorer to Coin. The plugin renames it CoinService and fills the name into the code.Write your code in the methods (delete the ones you don't need) and press Play.  Every button works the same way: select the folder, press the button, rename.  Button	Makes	Put it inService	game logic (...Service)	ServerScriptService › Services (server) or ReplicatedStorage › Services (both) Controller	client logic (...Controller)	ReplicatedStorage › Controllers Gui Controller	a controller for one ScreenGui	ReplicatedStorage › Controllers Network	Packet remote events	ReplicatedStorage › Network Binder	code for every part with a tag	ServerScriptService › Binders, ReplicatedStorage › Binders › Client or Shared Bound Class	a class for a Binder	next to the Binder Class / InheritedClass	an object class	ReplicatedStorage › Classes Input	an InputContext	ReplicatedStorage › Input Add Extras	an Assets folder that preloads, plus SFX and Music sound groups Update Script Name	renames the open script to the text you selected	  What every template does: Templates.  Let an AI write the modules Once Setup is done, an AI can add modules for you. See Install with AI.

searchDocs.title: Settings​
searchDocs.content: </> type Settings = Settings Every option with its default lives inSettings.luau and on the settings page.

searchDocs.title: Entry​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Entry { Folders: {Instance }-- where to look; every ModuleScript inside them (at any depth) is a candidate Predicate: ((module: ModuleScript ) → boolean)?-- only load modules this returns true for, e.g. Init.matchesName Order: number?-- only used when entries are a dictionary (the old Entries-module format): lower runs first } One group of modules to load. A ModuleScript inside another ModuleScript is never loaded on its own: it belongs to its parent, which can require it.

searchDocs.title: Entries​
searchDocs.content: </> type Entries = {Entry} | {[string]: Entry} A list of entries, loaded in list order. A dictionary of named entries (the format of the oldSharedEntries/ServerEntries modules) also works and is sorted by each entry's Order.

searchDocs.title: Modules​
searchDocs.content: </> type Modules = {[string]: any} Every loaded module's returned value, by the ModuleScript's name.

searchDocs.title: start​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Init.start( entries: Entries,-- what to load, in order settings: {[string]: any}?-- overrides for any of the settings ) → Promise<Modules,number,number> Loads and starts every module the entries point at. Call it once per realm: from one Script on the server and one LocalScript on the client. Load: requires the modules, entry by entry. Inside an entry, modules with a lower Priority attribute go first. Modules with an Ignore attribute, modules a Predicate turns down and ModuleScripts that sit inside another ModuleScript are skipped. Init: calls Init on each module, one at a time, in load order. If one errors or takes longer than InitTimeout, it's reported and that module won't Start. Start: calls Start on every module at once (a Start that waits doesn't hold up the others). Each module's hooks (OnPlayerAdded, OnHeartbeat, ...) connect as soon as its own Start returns. The returned promise resolves after every Start has returned (or hit StartTimeout), with the loaded modules by name, how many loaded, and how long it took in seconds. Init.start(entries):andThen(function(modules, count, seconds) workspace:SetAttribute("ServerStarted", true) end)

searchDocs.title: matchesName​
searchDocs.content: </> Init.matchesName(pattern: string) → (module: ModuleScript ) → boolean Makes a Predicate that keeps modules whose name matches astring pattern. { Folders = { ServerScriptService.Services }, Predicate = Init.matchesName("Service$") } -- names ending in Service

searchDocs.title: Install with Rojo + Wally
searchDocs.content: Install with Rojo + Wally Add Init to wally.toml: [dependencies] Init = "kashtheking/init@1.0.0" wally install, and map Packages to ReplicatedStorage.Packages in your project file. Add the boot scripts and folders. The example project has all of them; copy it, or start from it: git clone https://github.com/KashTheKing/init && cd init && rojo serve example.project.json ServerScriptService/InitServer.server.luauStarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/InitClient.client.luau Every folder a boot script names must exist. Git doesn't keep empty folders, so add a .gitkeep to each (Rojo ignores it) or declare them in the project file with "$className": "Folder". rojo serve, connect from Studio and press Play. Your folders, names and order are yours: change the entries in the boot scripts. See Entries. The templates are plain .luau files you can copy, and the plugin's template buttons work in Rojo games too.

searchDocs.title: Pick how to install​
searchDocs.content: Without code: the Init Framework plugin. Two clicks.With AI: paste one prompt into Claude, Cursor or ChatGPT.Rojo + Wally: kashtheking/init.Studio, by hand: drag in Init.rbxm.  Next: the lifecycle explains exactly when each method runs.

searchDocs.title: Copy this prompt​
searchDocs.content: Paste it into Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT or any AI that can read web pages:  Read https://kashtheking.com/init/SKILL.md and follow it. Set up the Init framework (kashtheking/init) in my Roblox game, then add a CoinService that gives every player 100 coins when they join and shows them on the leaderboard.   Change the second part to whatever you want built. After setup, you can keep asking: "add a ShopGuiController for my Shop ScreenGui", "add a LavaBinder that kills players who touch parts tagged Lava".

searchDocs.title: Claude Code​
searchDocs.content: Install the skill once and Claude uses it whenever you mention Init:  mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/init-framework && curl -L https://kashtheking.com/init/SKILL.md -o ~/.claude/skills/init-framework/SKILL.md   With the Roblox Studio MCP connected, Claude can create the modules in Studio and playtest. With a Rojo project, it edits files and runs wally install.

searchDocs.title: If your AI can't touch Studio​
searchDocs.content: Chat AIs (ChatGPT, Claude.ai) can't click in Studio. Do the setup with the plugin (two clicks), then ask the AI for module code and paste it into a module the plugin made.

searchDocs.title: Check the AI's work​
searchDocs.content: Press Play. The Output should say ✅ Initialized N Server modules and ✅ Initialized N Client modules. Anything that starts with [Init] is an error: paste it back to the AI. See Troubleshooting.

searchDocs.title: What behaves differently​
searchDocs.content: Every Init runs before any Start. The old loader ran Init then Start per module, so a Start could run before other modules' Init. If a Start relied on that, move the code into Init.Starts run at the same time. A slow Start no longer holds up the modules after it.Modules run in the order you list. The old loader required in order but called Init/Start in an arbitrary order.Modules inside a ModuleScript aren't loaded. The old one loaded them too, unless a predicate filtered them out.Step runs at 60 per second. The old one read Stepped's first argument (the game time) as the frame time, so it could run many extra steps per frame.A timed-out Init or Start keeps running. The old one cancelled it.Start errors are always reported (the old one only reported them with Verbose).

searchDocs.title: Settings
searchDocs.content: Settings Pass overrides as the second argument of Init.start. A name that isn't a setting is an error, so typos are caught. Init.start(entries, { Verbose = true, StartTimeout = 30 }) Setting	Default	WhatVerbose	false	log every module as it loads, inits and starts DefaultLogEnabled	true	log 🔲 Initializing and ✅ Initialized N modules DebugLabelFormat	"%s - %s"	MicroProfiler label for per-frame hooks (module, method) InitTimeout	3	seconds to wait for each Init StartTimeout	15	seconds to wait for each Start DefaultPriority	0	priority of modules without a Priority attribute IgnoreAttribute	"Ignore"	attribute that skips a module PriorityAttribute	"Priority"	attribute that orders modules The method names are settings too, if you'd rather call them something else: Setting	DefaultInitMethod	"Init" StartMethod	"Start" PlayerAdded	"OnPlayerAdded" PlayerRemoving	"OnPlayerRemoving" Accumulator	"Step" Heartbeat	"OnHeartbeat" Stepped	"OnStepped" RenderStepped	"OnRenderStepped" Died	"OnDied" CharacterAdded	"OnCharacterAdded" CharacterRemoving	"OnCharacterRemoving" Source: Settings.luau.

searchDocs.title: 1. Load​
searchDocs.content: Entries load in list order. Inside an entry, every ModuleScript in its Folders (at any depth) is required, lowest Priority attribute first, then in Explorer order. Skipped:  a ModuleScript inside another ModuleScript (it belongs to its parent, which can require it)a module whose Ignore attribute is truea module the entry's Predicate turns down (e.g. not ending in Service)  A module that errors while loading is reported and left out; the rest still load.

searchDocs.title: 2. Init: one at a time​
searchDocs.content: module:Init() runs for each module, in load order, and Init waits for each before the next. Use it for the module's own setup: tables, constants, instances it owns. Other modules may not have run their Init yet, so don't call into them here.  If Init errors or takes longer than InitTimeout (3 s), it's reported and that module doesn't Start or get hooks.

searchDocs.title: 3. Start: all at once​
searchDocs.content: After every Init has finished, module:Start() runs for every module, in load order, each in its own thread. A Start that waits (for a GUI, for data) doesn't hold up the others. This is where modules use each other.  If Start errors or runs longer than StartTimeout (15 s), it's reported. A Start that's still running keeps running; Init just stops waiting for it.

searchDocs.title: 4. Hooks​
searchDocs.content: As soon as a module's Start returns, its hooks connect:  Method	Runs	ArgsOnPlayerAdded	for each player already in game, then each player who joins	player OnPlayerRemoving	when a player leaves	player Step	exactly 60 times a second, however fast frames run	dt (1/60) OnHeartbeat	every RunService.Heartbeat	dt OnStepped	every RunService.Stepped	time, dt OnRenderStepped	client: every frame before render	dt OnCharacterAdded	client: local player's current and each new character	character OnCharacterRemoving	client: when the character is removed	character OnDied	client: when the local player's Humanoid dies	  Errors in a hook are reported and don't break the event. Per-frame hooks get a MicroProfiler label like CoinService - Step.

searchDocs.title: 5. Done​
searchDocs.content: The promise from Init.start resolves once every Start has returned (or timed out):  Init.start(entries):andThen(function(modules, count, seconds) print(modules.CoinService, count, seconds) end)

searchDocs.title: Using one module from another​
searchDocs.content: Modules are plain tables, and require returns the same table Init loaded:  local CoinService = require(ServerScriptService.Services.CoinService) function ShopService.Start(self) CoinService:Give(player, 10) -- fine: every Init has run end

searchDocs.title: A module never runs​
searchDocs.content: Its name doesn't match the entry's predicate: Coins isn't loaded by matchesName("Service$"); name it CoinService.It's inside another ModuleScript. Only top-level modules (folders are fine) load.It has the Ignore attribute.It's in a folder no entry lists, or on the wrong side (a Controller in ServerScriptService).Turn on Verbose = true to see every module Init loads.

searchDocs.title: Nothing prints at all​
searchDocs.content: The boot scripts aren't running: InitServer must be a Script in ServerScriptService and InitClient a LocalScript in StarterPlayerScripts, both enabled.

searchDocs.title: Binder​
searchDocs.content: Raw  --!strict -- A Binder (kashtheking/binder): runs code for every instance with a tag, and cleans up when it goes away. -- Install Trove and Binder from Wally or the plugin's "Add Packages". -- Put it in ServerScriptService/Binders (server), ReplicatedStorage/Binders/Client (client) or -- ReplicatedStorage/Binders/Shared (both). Init calls the binder's Start for you. -- This example pushes every part tagged "_SNIPPET_" forward at its "Speed" attribute. -- Binder docs: https://kashtheking.com/library/docs/packages/binder local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local RunService = game:GetService("RunService") local Binder = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Binder) local Trove = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Trove) -- Called for each matching instance. The trove is cleaned when the instance is unbound; -- anything you return with a :Destroy() method is cleaned too. local function _SNIPPET_(part: BasePart, trove: Trove.Trove, speed: number) trove:Connect(RunService.Heartbeat, function() part.AssemblyLinearVelocity = part.CFrame.LookVector * speed end) return trove end return Binder.new(_SNIPPET_, { Tags = { "_SNIPPET_" }, -- instances need one of these CollectionService tags ClassNames = { "BasePart" }, -- and must be one of these classes (optional) Ancestors = { workspace }, -- and must be inside one of these (optional) -- Last check (optional). Return true to bind; anything returned after true goes to the constructor. Predicate = function(instance: Instance) local speed = tonumber(instance:GetAttribute("Speed")) if not speed then warn(`[_SNIPPET_Binder] {instance:GetFullName()} needs a number "Speed" attribute`) return false end return true, speed end, })

searchDocs.title: BoundClass​
searchDocs.content: Raw  --!strict -- A class for a Binder to construct, one per bound instance: Binder.new(_SNIPPET_, { Tags = { "_SNIPPET_" } }). -- Put it next to the Binder that uses it. The Binder cleans the trove when the instance is unbound. local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Trove = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Trove) local _SNIPPET_ = {} _SNIPPET_.__index = _SNIPPET_ export type _SNIPPET_Properties = { Instance: Instance, Trove: Trove.Trove, } export type _SNIPPET_ = typeof(setmetatable({} :: _SNIPPET_Properties, _SNIPPET_)) export type ClassType = _SNIPPET_ -- Called by the Binder for each bound instance. Values your Binder's Predicate returns after `true` -- arrive as extra parameters after the trove. function _SNIPPET_.new(instance: Instance, trove: Trove.Trove): _SNIPPET_ local self = setmetatable( { Instance = instance, Trove = trove, } :: _SNIPPET_Properties, _SNIPPET_ ) return self end -- Called by the Binder when the instance is unbound function _SNIPPET_.Destroy(self: _SNIPPET_): () end return _SNIPPET_

searchDocs.title: Class​
searchDocs.content: Raw  --!strict -- A plain class (an object you make many of with .new). Init does NOT load classes; require them yourself. -- Put it in ReplicatedStorage/Classes (shared) or ServerScriptService/Classes (server-only). local _SNIPPET_ = {} _SNIPPET_.__index = _SNIPPET_ export type _SNIPPET_Properties = {} export type _SNIPPET_ = typeof(setmetatable({} :: _SNIPPET_Properties, _SNIPPET_)) export type ClassType = _SNIPPET_ -- Creates a new _SNIPPET_ function _SNIPPET_.new(): _SNIPPET_ local properties: _SNIPPET_Properties = {} local self = setmetatable(properties, _SNIPPET_) return self end -- Cleans up the _SNIPPET_ function _SNIPPET_.Destroy(self: _SNIPPET_): () end return _SNIPPET_

searchDocs.title: Controller​
searchDocs.content: Raw  --!strict -- A Controller: client-only game logic that Init loads and starts for you. Name it <Something>Controller. -- Put it in ReplicatedStorage/Controllers. Every method below is optional; delete the ones you don't use. local _SNIPPET_Controller = {} export type _SNIPPET_Controller = typeof(_SNIPPET_Controller) -- Runs first, one module at a time. Set up this module's own state here. -- Don't wait for other modules here (they may not have run Init yet); use Start for that. function _SNIPPET_Controller.Init(self: _SNIPPET_Controller) end -- Runs after every module's Init has finished. Safe to use other modules here. -- Waiting here is fine for a few seconds (StartTimeout is 15s); it doesn't hold up other modules. function _SNIPPET_Controller.Start(self: _SNIPPET_Controller) end ---- Runs for the local player's current character, then every time it respawns --function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnCharacterAdded(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, character: Model) -- --end ---- Runs when the local player's character is being removed --function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnCharacterRemoving(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, character: Model) -- --end ---- Runs when the local player's Humanoid dies --function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnDied(self: _SNIPPET_Controller) -- --end ---- Runs every frame before it renders (camera, UI that follows things) --function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnRenderStepped(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, dt: number) -- --end ---- Runs for every player already in the game (the local player too), then for every player who joins --function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnPlayerAdded(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, player: Player) -- --end ---- Runs when a player is leaving the game --function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnPlayerRemoving(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, player: Player) -- --end ---- Runs exactly 60 times a second, however fast the frames are --function _SNIPPET_Controller.Step(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, dt: number) -- --end ---- Runs every RunService.Heartbeat --function _SNIPPET_Controller.OnHeartbeat(self: _SNIPPET_Controller, dt: number) -- --end return _SNIPPET_Controller

searchDocs.title: GuiController​
searchDocs.content: Raw  --!strict -- A Controller for one ScreenGui. Name the ScreenGui in StarterGui "_SNIPPET_" (or change the name below). -- Put it in ReplicatedStorage/Controllers. It's a normal Controller with the GUI lookup done for you. local Players = game:GetService("Players") local player = assert(Players.LocalPlayer, "_SNIPPET_GuiController must be required on the client") local PlayerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui") :: PlayerGui -- Gives you autocomplete for the ScreenGui's children (works when the ScreenGui exists in StarterGui) export type Gui = typeof(game:GetService("StarterGui")["_SNIPPET_"]) local _SNIPPET_GuiController = { Gui = (nil :: any) :: Gui, } export type _SNIPPET_GuiController = typeof(_SNIPPET_GuiController) -- The ScreenGui is copied into PlayerGui when the player spawns, which can take a moment, so wait for it in Start function _SNIPPET_GuiController.Start(self: _SNIPPET_GuiController) self.Gui = assert( PlayerGui:WaitForChild("_SNIPPET_", 5) :: any, `[_SNIPPET_GuiController] the ScreenGui "_SNIPPET_" didn't appear in PlayerGui` ) end return _SNIPPET_GuiController

searchDocs.title: InheritedClass​
searchDocs.content: Raw  --!strict -- A class that inherits from another class. Insert it as a child of the parent class's ModuleScript. -- Init does NOT load classes; require them yourself. local SuperClass = require(script.Parent) local _SNIPPET_ = setmetatable({}, SuperClass) _SNIPPET_.__index = _SNIPPET_ export type _SNIPPET_ = typeof(_SNIPPET_) & SuperClass.ClassType & { __super: SuperClass.ClassType, } export type ClassType = _SNIPPET_ -- Creates a new _SNIPPET_; arguments go to the parent class's .new function _SNIPPET_.new(...: any): _SNIPPET_ local super = SuperClass.new(...) local self: _SNIPPET_ = setmetatable(super :: any, _SNIPPET_) :: any self.__super = super return self end return _SNIPPET_

searchDocs.title: Network​
searchDocs.content: Raw  --!strict -- Network packets, made with kashtheking/packet (install it from Wally or the plugin's "Add Packages"). -- Put it in ReplicatedStorage/Network. Init loads Network first on both sides, so every packet exists -- before anything sends one. Docs: https://kashtheking.com/library/docs/packages/packet local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Packet = require(ReplicatedStorage.Packages.Packet) return { -- Packet.new(name, ...types). Use exact types (Packet.NumberU8, Packet.String, ...) for smaller packets. _SNIPPET_ = Packet.new("_SNIPPET_", Packet.Any), }

searchDocs.title: Service​
searchDocs.content: Raw  --!strict -- A Service: game logic that Init loads and starts for you. Name it <Something>Service. -- Server-only: ServerScriptService/Services. Shared (runs on server AND client): ReplicatedStorage/Services. -- Every method below is optional; delete the ones you don't use. local _SNIPPET_Service = {} export type _SNIPPET_Service = typeof(_SNIPPET_Service) -- Runs first, one module at a time. Set up this module's own state here. -- Don't wait for other modules here (they may not have run Init yet); use Start for that. function _SNIPPET_Service.Init(self: _SNIPPET_Service) end -- Runs after every module's Init has finished. Safe to use other modules here. -- Waiting here is fine for a few seconds (StartTimeout is 15s); it doesn't hold up other modules. function _SNIPPET_Service.Start(self: _SNIPPET_Service) end ---- Runs for every player already in the game, then for every player who joins --function _SNIPPET_Service.OnPlayerAdded(self: _SNIPPET_Service, player: Player) -- --end ---- Runs when a player is leaving the game --function _SNIPPET_Service.OnPlayerRemoving(self: _SNIPPET_Service, player: Player) -- --end ---- Runs exactly 60 times a second, however fast the frames are (good for game ticks) --function _SNIPPET_Service.Step(self: _SNIPPET_Service, dt: number) -- --end ---- Runs every RunService.Heartbeat --function _SNIPPET_Service.OnHeartbeat(self: _SNIPPET_Service, dt: number) -- --end ---- Runs every RunService.Stepped (before physics) --function _SNIPPET_Service.OnStepped(self: _SNIPPET_Service, time: number, dt: number) -- --end return _SNIPPET_Service
